content:
According to 9to5Mac's web traffic analysis, Apple is testing an iPhone version of iOS 27.0.1. The update is expected to focus on bug fixes and performance improvements.

iOS 27.0.1 is coming soon

iOS 27.0.1 began surfacing in 9to5Mac's traffic analytics a few days ago. MacRumors has also reported the same situation.

9to5Mac this morning cited Apple as saying it will release a software update early next week to fix an issue where some iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max devices reboot after a failed Face ID recognition.

We reported on this issue a few days ago, explaining that it occurs when you try to use Face ID to open apps such as "Passwords." If Face ID fails, your iPhone may suddenly restart.

My iPhone 18 Pro or iPhone 18 Pro Max has never experienced this issue, but clearly a number of users are affected. The good news is that this bug can be fixed with software, not a hardware fault.

iOS 27.0.1 is likely to address the above issue, though this has yet to be confirmed. The update may also include other bug fixes affecting iOS 27 and the new iPhone 18 Pro hardware.

Have you encountered any issues since upgrading to iOS 27? Or any iPhone 18 Pro-specific problems? Feel free to let us know in the comments.
